text: 🇲🇽✊ "Where does that money come from? How is it that the government can now support people and before it couldn't? Because now taxes are collected from those who must pay them, and now there is no robbing." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, La Concordia, Chiapas "Before, there were no scholarships for girls, boys, young people. At most a few for a select few. The vote was requested in exchange for support. Not now. Now it is universal." In Chiapas every public school student, from primary through university, now has a scholarship. The universal pension for older adults, begun in 2019, and the pension for people with disabilities are constitutional rights, and the pension must rise above inflation every year. More than 400,000 farmers receive Sembrando Vida. "That is the Fourth Transformation of public life."

🇲🇽✊ "Abroad they boasted that the only opportunity Mexico had was to offer cheap labor. Not how good Mexican workers were, not the culture of Mexicans. To foreign investment, they offered cheap labor." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, La Concordia, Chiapas At the Rizo de Oro bridge on November 7, she said La Angostura dam was finished in 1976: "a hydroelectric plant was built for the well-being of Mexico, but the people were forgotten." She named the six presidents of the neoliberal period, 1982 to 2018: De la Madrid, Salinas, Zedillo, Fox, Calderón, Peña Nieto. "The minimum wage did not rise." Public companies were sold to a few at the top. From 1943 to 1982, about 27,000 IMSS hospital beds were built; in the following 36 years, only 4,000. "We must not forget it, because a people without memory has no compass."
banner: "A PEOPLE WITHOUT MEMORY HAS NO COMPASS"

text: 🇲🇽✊ "They could not travel by road because they were afraid of the people. They thought that reaching the presidency meant moving away from the people. And we think the opposite." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas "The presidents of long ago did not do this. They stayed locked up in the president's house of the time, which was Los Pinos." When they went out, they were surrounded by the Estado Mayor Presidencial: "8,000 soldiers dedicated to guarding the president." Los Pinos became a museum open to the public when López Obrador took office. Sheinbaum tours the states every Friday to Sunday, sometimes from Thursday: "The job of a president is to listen, attend and resolve." This weekend: Chiapa de Corzo and Ocozocoautla on Friday, then on Saturday the Rizo de Oro bridge, three hours from Tuxtla, and the scholarship event in Suchiapa.

🇲🇽🎨 "In all of Latin America, those who led independence were criollo military men... But in Mexico, independence was commanded by a village priest, Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, and his disciple José María Morelos y Pavón. They did not only fight for independence, they fought for social justice." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas At the Universidad Politécnica de Chiapas on November 7, she told students that Morelos wrote a Constitution, Apatzingán's, that never took effect but is the basis of the 1917 Constitution. In it: "Education must be the same for the son of the hacendado as for the son of the peon." "We must moderate indigence and opulence." And the sovereignty of the homeland "did not lie in a few, but resided in the people of Mexico." "There is no country in the world like ours."

🇲🇽🚆 "They told him, 'Mr. President, from here we have to go on horseback, because there is no road.' And he said, 'How is it possible that the state of Chiapas is not connected?'" — Governor Eduardo Ramírez, La Concordia, Chiapas Opening the Rizo de Oro bridge, the governor recalled that in 1940 President Lázaro Cárdenas toured Oaxaca and then Chiapas, riding on horseback all the way to the Soconusco. Out of that trip came the Pan-American Highway through Chiapas to Central America. Then in the 1970s the La Angostura dam flooded the old town of La Concordia and split the families of the Sierra from those of the Frailesca. For decades they asked for bridges. "Many years had to pass for Chiapas to become the national priority." From Chicomuselo to Tuxtla, a trip of more than 5 hours will now take about 2.5.

🇲🇽🚆 "We deliver today the Rizo de Oro bridge, a work awaited for more than 50 years, that closes a time of isolation, of long distances, of inequality." — Jesús Antonio Esteva, Secretary of Infrastructure, La Concordia, Chiapas More than 300,000 people in 10 municipalities and 21 communities of the Frailesca and Sierra Mariscal crossed the reservoir on homemade rafts, "chalanas," often for over an hour and sometimes not at all when it rained: "they crossed their harvests, they crossed the sick, always at the risk of their lives." Sheinbaum: a crossing of one or two hours now takes five minutes. Together with the La Concordia bridge, opened by López Obrador in 2024, travel on state route 230 between Tuxtla Gutiérrez and Frontera Comalapa drops from 6.5 hours to 4. Local leader Ramiro Ruiz thanked her for "20 years of struggle" made real.
banner: RIZO DE ORO: A 50-YEAR WAIT ENDS

text: 🇲🇽🚆 "Today's inauguration carries one word. Beyond the great work, because it is a work of Mexican engineering, after many years of abandonment of Mexican engineering too... it is a word that the Fourth Transformation of public life brought with it: justice. And alongside that word goes the word well-being." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, La Concordia, Chiapas On November 7 she opened the Rizo de Oro bridge over the La Angostura reservoir. Infrastructure Secretary Jesús Antonio Esteva: 408 m long, 2 km with its road accesses, the first mixed steel-and-concrete arch bridge in Mexico, built by Mexican companies. 27 steel segments of about 100 tons each were mounted by cableway from 93 m temporary towers. It generated 5,700 jobs. Load-tested with the UNAM Engineering Institute and the Mexican Transport Institute, it will be instrumented to monitor deformations in real time. Begun under López Obrador, finished under Sheinbaum.

🇲🇽🎨 "Education is a right. Education is not a commodity. Education is not a privilege that only those with economic resources can pay for." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ocozocoautla, Chiapas In Ocozocoautla on November 6, she recalled the 1986–87 UNAM student movement: the rector's reform raised tuition and fees, and a propaganda campaign called students lazy. Students demanded a public debate, broadcast on Radio Universidad, chanted that slogan by the tens of thousands, filled the Zócalo and struck until the authorities repealed every reform. "40 years later, and I never imagined I would be president of the Republic, we defend the same thing." She traced the right to public education to José María Morelos, Benito Juárez and the Mexican Revolution, "and who else defends public education? You, the young people of Mexico."

🇲🇽🎨 "You open TikTok and start swiping at the screen. And suddenly an hour has passed. And suddenly two hours. It is a form of addiction. It is like a drug." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas At the National Day for Peace on November 6, she said her government studied why depression and anxiety have risen among young people who lived the COVID lockdown in primary school and then the boom of social media and artificial intelligence. They spoke with engineers, many of them Mexican, who left very high-paying positions at Meta and TikTok "because they realized that the creation of the algorithms asks those who create them to generate addiction." Even much of the content is now made with AI: "It is not even created by a person anymore." Her response: talk about it in schools with the ABC of Emotions.
📸 Becas para el Bienestar — Ocozocoautla de Espinosa, Chiapas, 6 de noviembre de 2026
